document: General Theta Foundations I — R77 mathematical dependency additions
evidence_type: author-written proofs, author-team AI challenges and finite diagnostics; not formal verification, independent human review or editorial assessment
numbering_policy: Numbers and pages must be merged from actual main/supplement native auxiliary output; no displayed numbering is guessed here.
proof_graph_policy: Dependencies are mathematical premises. Comparison/counterexample references and literature ingredients are recorded separately where needed.
source_identity_limit: Integrated source hashes and final source commit are supplied by final source-bound receipts. Development snapshots do not predeclare those identities.

statements.label: thm:r77-shared-normal-form
statements.title: Shared normal form and exact initialization charge
assumptions: finite group
finite preparations and outcomes
closed convex constraint for every command word
common transitions and decoder
no uncounted preparation label available to decoder
statements.proof_mechanism: One identity-word projection for all starts; distinct mixed projected rows inject into distinct transient initial labels.
excluded_inferences: no free preparation identity for the decoder
no test of only one representative word per group element
no faithful-action requirement

statements.label: thm:r77-shared-polytope
statements.title: Invariant-polytope resource formulas
assumptions: finite group
finite exact preparation family
polytope lies in full probability response space
statements.proof_mechanism: Vertex reduction and exact accounting for prescribed nonvertices, including nonextreme recurrent profiles.
excluded_inferences: the containing polytope need not stay in the target span
no polynomial-time global synthesis claim
do not charge an already counted nonvertex profile twice

statements.label: lem:r77-joint-multiplicity
statements.title: Joint multiplicity
assumptions: finite group
joint module generated by all preparation residuals
statements.proof_mechanism: Independent group-algebra coefficients give a sum of Fourier column spaces, represented by horizontal concatenation.
excluded_inferences: joint rank is not the maximum individual rank
joint rank may exceed the irreducible degree

statements.label: thm:r77-shared-low-contrast
statements.title: Exact noncyclic memory at small common contrast
assumptions: finite group
all preparation group means equal
sufficiently small positive contrast with explicit t0
statements.proof_mechanism: Simultaneous centered preparations and one bounded decoder attain the complete joint multiplicity cover.
excluded_inferences: common mean cannot be removed unconditionally
no general high-contrast equality
no universal pure-start surcharge

statements.label: thm:r77-joint-robust
statements.title: Joint robust multiplicity certificate
assumptions: uniform total variation bound for every preparation and every word
weights nonnegative with sum one
statements.proof_mechanism: Weighted concatenation retains sqrt(2) delta operator error independently of the number of preparation blocks.
excluded_inferences: no multiplicative error factor from the number of preparations
no automatic pure initializer
not necessarily a sharp error law

statements.label: prop:r77-shared-involution
statements.title: Unbounded joint multiplicity for a fixed group
assumptions: G=C2
q preparations
q+1 outcomes
0<epsilon<1/(q+1)
statements.proof_mechanism: Exact 2q shared memory versus two labels per separate preparation, with a rational strictly positive response and explicit robust threshold.
excluded_inferences: strict positivity is asserted for target responses, not permutation transition entries

statements.label: prop:r77-many-initializers
statements.title: An unbounded pure initialization cost
assumptions: G=C2
binary terminal output
r distinct positive preparation amplitudes below 1/2
statements.proof_mechanism: Mixed core two and exact pure count r+1; positivity of every initial decoder row excludes a controller with only r labels.
excluded_inferences: does not contradict the inherited single-preparation initializer theorem

statements.label: lem:r77-robust-antichain
statements.title: Robust antichain factorization certificate
assumptions: J probability rows lambda_n on M labels
arbitrary decoder columns d_m in [0,1]^M
diagonal responses at most epsilon and off-diagonal responses at least 0<b<=1
epsilon<b^2/(2M^2)
statements.proof_mechanism: Threshold at b/(2M). An off-diagonal sum has one summand at least b/M; the diagonal bound forces that coordinate outside the other thresholded support. Ordered witnesses give an antichain. A random-permutation proof gives the central-binomial bound.
statements.conclusion: J<=binom(M,floor(M/2)); all equal-size subsets give a sharp abstract cardinality example.
excluded_inferences: no Born, quantum-state or decoder-linearity assumption
abstract extremality is not a chronological qubit simulator
the exact support-antichain argument is classical

statements.label: thm:r77-operational-antichain
statements.title: Memory lower bound from approximately exposing tests
assumptions: J causal preparation procedures with observable herald probabilities p_n>=p_*>0
terminal test and its future policy code unavailable before the herald
fixed decoder depends only on counted current label and requested test
own-test rejection zero and cross-test rejection at least 0<s<=1
each specified experiment has target expected cost at most B
TV approximation of every complete stopped record at error delta
statements.proof_mechanism: Joint-event TV controls herald mass and herald-plus-rejection mass before normalization. Causality gives one conditional hidden-label row shared by all later tests. Diagonal response is at most 2delta/p_* and cross response at least s/2, leaving a strict factor-two margin in the antichain condition.
statements.conclusion: delta<=p_*s^2/(32M^2) implies J<=binom(M,floor(M/2)); delta<=p_*s^2/(32J^2) implies M>=a(J).
excluded_inferences: both mixed and pure starts without an extra pure surcharge
no uncounted-history decoder access
no unconditional-to-conditional TV shortcut

statements.label: thm:r77-unrestricted-qubit
statements.title: Unrestricted finite certificates and arithmetic rates
assumptions: undamped R75 qubit instrument with initial I/2 and fixed Bloch angle theta
visible adaptive stopped experiments with target expected calls at most fixed B>0
cost-free terminal POVMs and no additional entangled register
arbitrary causal classical decoder tables with no advance access to later terminal requests
non-root phase for separated finite certificates; original z=(3+4i)/5 or stated badly-approximable hypothesis for explicit growth
statements.proof_mechanism: Early-abort prefixes 1 0^n have controlled target cost and prepare pure orbit states. Terminal complement projectors expose them with separation s_J. Integer real numerators give exponential separation for the original phase; a separate sine/Diophantine argument handles badly approximable phases. Inherited orbit-seed dictionaries give the upper.
statements.conclusion: delta<=zeta*8^(-J)*s_J^2/(32J^2) gives both unrestricted classical minima at least a(J). At the original phase delta<=25*zeta/(128*200^J*J^2) suffices. Fixed-B growth has liminf coefficient at least one relative to log_2 log_8(1/delta) in the stated arithmetic cases.
excluded_inferences: unrestricted log-log lower does not match the logarithmic upper
no badly-approximable assertion for the original angle
no report-only approximate lower
no additional pure-start lower
no simulator expected-duration bound or continuum-command rate

dependency_roles.thm:r76-physical-logarithm: inherited orbit-seed upper and physical comparison only; its restricted lower is not exported

statements.label: cor:r77-algebraic-unrestricted
statements.title: Every non-root algebraic phase has the same lower order
assumptions: algebraic unit phase z not a root of unity
same causal qubit simulation and fixed-B assumptions as the preceding theorem
degree D and integer A>0 with Az integral
H>=max(2,A^D product_(j=2)^D max(1,|z_j|))
statements.proof_mechanism: The norm of the nonzero algebraic integer A^q(z^q-1) is a nonzero integer. Bounding the other conjugates gives exponential separation; substitute it in the preceding finite certificate.
statements.conclusion: s_J>=4^(-D)*H^(-2(J-1)); delta<=zeta*H^4/[32*16^D*(8H^4)^J*J^2] implies N_cl>=a(J), and the fixed-B log-log liminf coefficient is at least one.
excluded_inferences: no polynomial Diophantine separation or sharp exponent
no matching unrestricted logarithmic lower
classical_ingredients: integrality and multiplicativity of algebraic norms

statements.label: thm:r77-reset-cover
statements.title: Exact optimal-memory formula with ties
assumptions: finite-dimensional finite-command reset instrument I_ai(rho)=tr(E_ai rho)sigma_i
every failure effect E_ai is positive definite
no closed failure set
positive bounded call-cost operators
success requires immediate commitment and no extra free observation/measurement/reset
fixed-program autonomous controller with prescribed counted pure start and inherited terminal-decoder convention
statements.proof_mechanism: An optimal first row lies in P_*. At a dual maximizing preparation all first failure reports are exposed; residual equality forces a continuing row supported on each optimal-action set. One support action per used row yields a transversal. Conversely pure transversal rows and deterministic post-report routing give Bellman equality and properness from the cost floor.
statements.conclusion: m_*=1+min_(p in P_*)t([s]\I(p)); arbitrary ties and stochastic transitions do not improve it. Event stopping uses m_* total labels and state stopping m_*+1. Algebraic data admit a finite exact procedure.
excluded_inferences: not arbitrary nonreset back-action or inaccessible reports
no action-uniqueness assumption
no polynomial-time algorithm or executed general elimination

dependency_roles.thm:reset-control: finite Bellman vector, proper optimal selector, primal/dual attainment

statements.label: thm:r77-reset-gap
statements.title: Attained certificate of a strict optimality gap
assumptions: all reset-cover assumptions
M>=1 live labels
robustly proper controller; infinite worst-state cost satisfies the lower trivially
statements.proof_mechanism: Keep only the first post-failure residual minimum over M rows to form K_M. Minimize its largest eigenvalue over a compact product of simplexes. Zero gap and strict exposure force every residual minimum to vanish, giving an optimal controller with those rows. An optimal row family gives the converse.
statements.conclusion: Worst-state cost>=V_*+D_M; D_M is attained and D_M>0 iff M<m_*. Algebraic data give finite exact computability.
excluded_inferences: D_M is a lower certificate, not the full constrained cost frontier
not the original squared-sign minimax-risk gap
floating optimization does not certify exact zeros

statements.label: thm:r77-reset-universality
statements.title: Universality of the optimal-memory covering problem
assumptions: q>=2 actions and finite nonempty proper sets A_i subset [q]
fixed rational 0<r<1
intermediate basis outcome and realized cost are not observations at the controller port
statements.proof_mechanism: Use s+q basis states, reset effects (r/s)I, and diagonal costs in [1,4] encoding the optimal sets. The constant Bellman vector and additional basis coordinates give spectral value 3+r/(1-r)+max_j p_j, uniquely minimized by the uniform row. Exact memory is the transversal number plus one. Polynomial encoding length yields an explicit classical transversal reduction.
statements.conclusion: V_*=3+r/(1-r)+1/q and m_*=t+1 for an actual rational reset experiment with positive effects and constant success probability; exact optimal memory is NP-hard on this family.
excluded_inferences: only cost/effect operators commute; CP maps need not commute
no claim resolving P versus NP
not a generic POMDP hardness assertion

statements.label: ex:r77-reset-exposure
statements.title: Why positive reachability cannot be dropped
assumptions: two-dimensional Hilbert space and one reset state |0><0|
E_a=E_b=diag(1/2,0)
G_a=diag(1,6) and G_b=diag(2,5)
failure effects are semidefinite, not definite
statements.proof_mechanism: Direct Bellman and diagonal calculations give v=2, L_a=diag(2,6), L_b=diag(3,5), robust value five and unique initial action b. Constant b has cost operator diag(4,5) and one label; its worst-case state never sees the reset report.
statements.conclusion: Without positive exposure the all-reset cover expression would give two labels while one is robustly optimal.
excluded_inferences: does not contradict the reset-cover theorem at its hypotheses
not a classification of all semidefinite-effect experiments
